headline: Futures edge up as Brent slides toward $110; bitcoin steady near $80,400
summary: Bitcoin is about $80,370 at 8:35 a.m. Monday, flat over 24 hours and down 2.4% on the week, and ether is about $2,329; total crypto value is about $2.71 trillion, Bitcoin's share is 59.5% and Fear & Greed is a neutral 50, with Quant (+22%), AKEDO (+10%), MemeCore (+9%) and Ethena (+6%) leading the top 100 and Bitway (-14%) lagging. U.S. stock futures are modestly higher (S&P 500 +0.2%, Dow +0.4% at about 8 a.m., per AP) and TSX futures are up about 0.3% as oil keeps falling on Iran diplomacy, with U.S. crude down about 2.2% near $101 and Brent down to about $110 from Friday's $116.72 settle, while gold is up about 0.6% near $4,032. Verizon's profit beat and raised outlook lead early earnings news, AI cloud stocks such as CoreWeave are lower premarket, and Wednesday's Fed and Bank of Canada decisions plus Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon results are the week's main events.

crypto.label: Cautious
crypto.why: Bitcoin is holding just above $80,000 after a dip under it overnight but remains below its 50-day average (about $81,800) before the Fed, and the Fear & Greed index is a neutral 50 rather than fearful.

stocks.label: Mixed
stocks.why: Friday's drop left the S&P 500 and TSX at two-week lows with the 10-year yield near 5% and the VIX near 19, but futures are slightly higher Monday as Brent falls about 6% from Friday's settle on Iran diplomacy and Verizon's raised outlook gives earnings week a firm start.

drivers.title: AI-spending doubts hit Big Tech and chips
drivers.detail: Meta closed down 7% Thursday despite beating forecasts as investors weighed its $135–$145 billion spending plan; AMD, Amazon, Nvidia and Broadcom fell 4–8%, and Friday's bounce in chips was partial. Early Monday the doubts spread to Asia, where Tokyo Electron and Renesas fell more than 3% and the Kospi later fell about 1.6%, per Investing.com and XTB, ahead of Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon results this week; premarket Monday, AI cloud providers CoreWeave, Iren and Nebius fell 4–5% even as Elon Musk said SpaceX raised $40 billion of debt to buy Nvidia chips, per AP.

drivers.title: Yields climb back to 5%
drivers.detail: After its biggest one-day drop in more than a year Thursday, the 10-year Treasury yield closed Friday near 4.99% as oil revives inflation worries; the University of Michigan survey shows year-ahead inflation expectations up to 4.7%. CME FedWatch data show about a 91% chance the Fed holds on Oct. 28, but roughly 80% odds of a hike in December, per FXStreet.

drivers.title: Iran: no weekend strike, oil eases
drivers.detail: The weekend passed without U.S. strikes on Iran, and Qatari mediators plus delegations from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey are in Tehran trying to head off renewed fighting, per Reuters and AP; U.S. crude was down about 2.2% near $101 at 8:35 a.m. Monday and Brent about 1.6% lower near $110 after settling at $116.72 Friday, its highest since June 2022. Trump says it is getting to be decision time on a strike or a deal, and the Houthis say they will keep targeting Saudi Arabia, so any attack on Gulf energy sites could quickly reverse the drop.

drivers.title: Telecoms: SpaceX threat meets Verizon beat
drivers.detail: AT&T and T-Mobile fell nearly 8% and Verizon about 1% after Bloomberg reported SpaceX is in talks for access to at least 80,000 U.S. cell sites, a step toward a fourth national carrier. Verizon's results Monday morning, with 406,000 net new phone subscribers and a raised outlook, are the first test of whether the big carriers can keep growing despite that threat.

drivers.title: Bitcoin pinned near $80,000 before the Fed
drivers.detail: Bitcoin fell nearly 2% to about $79,800 in Asian trading Monday as traders cut risk before Wednesday's Fed meeting, where a hint of a December rate hike would tighten the money flowing into risky assets, per CoinDesk; it is back near $80,370 at 8:35 a.m. About $810 million of leveraged bets were forcibly closed over the weekend, and the $80,000–$81,500 zone is where Glassnode estimates ETF and corporate buyers paid on average.

drivers.title: Bank of Canada rate hike now likely
drivers.detail: Swap markets price about 80% odds of a Bank of Canada hike to 2.50% on Oct. 28 after strong retail sales and Governor Macklem's warning on oil-driven inflation. The loonie is about 71.4 U.S. cents at 8:35 a.m. Monday, and a Reuters poll finds most economists expect a quarter-point hike,, near a one-month high, while RBC and TD each slipped about 0.4%.

crypto.name: Bitcoin
crypto.move: Up 0.1% in 24h, down 2.4% this week, at about $80,370 (down 4.5% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitcoin slipped through $80,000 Saturday morning, its first trip below that level since Oct. 15, and bottomed near $79,150 after the Wall Street Journal reported the U.S. was pulling personnel out of Middle East embassies and bases over intelligence that Iran was preparing attacks, per CoinDesk. BeInCrypto noted Trump had said the U.S. could strike Iran as soon as Sunday or strike a deal instead; neither has happened yet. Bitcoin recovered to about $80,400 Sunday afternoon, slipped to about $79,900 late Sunday then fell nearly 2% to about $79,800 in Asian trading Monday as traders cut risk before the Fed, per CoinDesk, and is about $80,370 at 8:35 a.m. (flat over 24 hours); Trump said Sunday afternoon there would be no strike today, with reports tying the rebound to positioning ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision rather than any specific news. About $810 million of leveraged crypto bets were liquidated (forcibly closed when losses ate through the trader's deposit) over 24 hours, mostly bullish bets, per CoinGlass data cited by Investing.com, and U.S. spot ETFs lost about $636 million on Thursday alone, their largest one-day outflow since June. Bitcoin remains below its 50-day average (about $81,800).
crypto.meaning: Glassnode estimates ETF buyers and corporate treasuries bought, on average, between about $80,000 and $81,500, so bitcoin is sitting right on the price where many big holders break even; a sustained drop below it would put them at a loss and could prompt more selling. Weekend moves on thin volume often get tested when bigger players return Monday, and the Iran decision could swing it either way before then. It is still about 39% above its July 1 low of $57,850.

outlook.bullCase: A U.S.–Iran deal or calmer Gulf headlines, plus ETF inflows returning Monday, could lift it back above $81,800 (the 50-day average) and $82,600 (the 20-day average), putting $84,000–$85,000 back in view.
outlook.bearCase: A daily close below $80,000, a U.S. strike on Iran that sends oil higher, more ETF outflows, or a hawkish Fed on Oct. 28 could extend the slide toward about $77,600 (Glassnode's 'true market mean', an estimate of the average holder's cost) and then the 100-day average near $75,300.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds above $80,000 through the U.S. session, CoinDesk's $82,500 level (Thursday's lost floor), any U.S. action or deal on Iran, oil, Monday's ETF flow data, the Fed decision on Oct. 28, and about $11 billion of bitcoin options expiring Oct. 30.

crypto.name: Ethereum
crypto.move: Up 0.1% in 24h, down 3.8% this week, at about $2,329 (down 13.2% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Ether fell with bitcoin's break below $80,000 Saturday morning, dropping as low as about $2,290, fell nearly 3% to just above $2,300 in Asian trading Monday, per CoinDesk, and is about $2,329 (up 0.1% over 24 hours) at 8:35 a.m., still under the $2,400 level that had supported it for about a week. Leveraged ether bets were hit almost as hard as bitcoin's (about $188 million liquidated over 24 hours versus $240 million for bitcoin, per CoinGlass data cited by The Crypto Times), even though ether is less than a fifth of bitcoin's size. Ether ETFs saw outflows on 14 of 17 trading days in October, about $1.2 billion in all, and developers on Friday postponed a test of the next big upgrade, Glamsterdam, after security researchers flagged a risk to existing smart contracts, per CoinDesk.
crypto.meaning: Ether is lagging bitcoin because big investors keep pulling money from the ETFs. Until those flows turn, rallies may be harder to sustain.

outlook.bullCase: Climbing back above $2,400, with ETF outflows stopping, could open a move toward $2,500 and then about $2,700, where October began.
outlook.bearCase: Holding below $2,300 with continued ETF outflows and more forced selling could send it toward $2,150–$2,200, and a broader risk-off turn could push it lower.
outlook.watch: Daily ether ETF flows, the $2,300 and $2,400 levels, the ETH/BTC ratio, and any new Glamsterdam upgrade timeline.

crypto.name: XRP
crypto.move: Up 0.2% in 24h, down 0.8% this week, at about $1.30 (down 16.6% over 30 days)
crypto.why: XRP is one of the few large coins in the green this weekend. CoinDesk reported Saturday that Franklin Templeton on Thursday put about $150 million more of its tokenized money-market fund (sgBENJI, a fund whose shares exist as tokens on a blockchain) onto the XRP Ledger, taking the fund's holdings there to nearly 193 million shares, worth roughly $200 million. All of the new shares sit in a single wallet linked to Franklin's issuing account, and it is not clear whether they belong to one investor or several.
crypto.meaning: A big asset manager using the XRP Ledger for tokenized funds supports the network's case for real-world finance, but the fund tokens don't require anyone to buy XRP, so the price link is indirect. XRP is still down about 14% over the past month, so this is a small bounce inside a larger slide.

outlook.bullCase: More tokenized-fund news and a steadier bitcoin above $80,000 could lift XRP back toward $1.40–$1.45.
outlook.bearCase: If bitcoin loses $80,000 again or the wider market turns risk-off after the Fed, XRP could slip back toward $1.20–$1.25.
outlook.watch: Whether Franklin clarifies who holds the new fund shares, bitcoin's hold on $80,000, and the Oct. 28 Fed decision.

crypto.name: Monero
crypto.why: Monero is giving back some recent gains, down about 2% over the past day at about $589 while most of the top 20 sit flat or lower, as traders rotate into privacy coins (coins that hide who sent what to whom), a theme that has also lifted Zcash this week. It ran about 19% in the week to Oct. 22, briefly topping $650 for a nine-month high near $645, as futures bets rebuilt (open interest, the value of open futures contracts, rose about 22% in coin terms from Oct. 15 to Oct. 20, per Santiment data cited by The Crypto Times), then gave some of that back in Saturday's sell-off before this weekend's partial rebound. Veteran trader Peter Brandt also drew attention by comparing its chart to silver's before its big run, though he gave no target.
crypto.meaning: Monero is moving on its own story rather than with bitcoin, which helps when the rest of the market is weak but also means sharp swings both ways. It remains about 23% below its January record near $799, and analysts at 24/7 Wall St. flag that the rising futures leverage looks like the build-up before its steep January drop.

outlook.bullCase: A close back above $650, the level that capped last week's rally, with privacy-coin demand holding up, could open a run toward $700 and later the $799 record.
outlook.bearCase: If leveraged bets unwind as they did in January, or bitcoin breaks lower, it could slip back under $580 and toward the mid-$500s where this month's rally began.
outlook.watch: The $650 level, futures open interest and funding rates, Zcash's moves (the two have traded together), and any exchange delisting or regulatory news on privacy coins.

crypto.name: Quant
crypto.move: Up 22.3% in 24h, up 7.2% this week, at about $223 (up 103% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Quant makes software (its Overledger platform) that lets banks move tokenized money, meaning bank deposits recorded on a blockchain-style ledger, between different systems. The token roughly doubled over the past month after The Clearing House, the payments company owned by big U.S. banks, picked Quant's technology in late September for a project to settle tokenized deposits over its existing payment rails, with rollout targeted for the first half of 2027; seven big UK banks also made the first live customer payments with tokenized sterling on infrastructure Quant built, per CoinMarketCap. It is the top gainer in the top 100 over the latest 24 hours, up about 13% to roughly $202, and we could not find a fresh announcement behind Monday's jump.
crypto.meaning: QNT is trading on a real business story, bank adoption of tokenized money, rather than pure hype, but the actual rollout is still more than six months away and banks paying for software does not automatically mean demand for the token. After a near doubling in a month, much of the good news may already be in the price.

outlook.bullCase: More bank or payments-network announcements, or a broader recovery in crypto, could carry it past about $210–$225 on continued momentum.
outlook.bearCase: Profit-taking after a roughly 96% monthly gain, or a wider crypto sell-off if bitcoin loses $80,000, could pull it back toward the $175–$180 area or lower.
outlook.watch: Any new partnership news from The Clearing House or UK banks, whether trading volume stays high, and bitcoin's direction around the Fed decision.

crypto.name: MemeCore
crypto.move: Up 9.3% in 24h, up 39.2% this week, at about $1.00 (down 17.7% over 30 days)
crypto.why: MemeCore, a blockchain built around meme coins, was the biggest decliner among about 90 large coins tracked by TokenPost on Sunday morning, falling to about $0.92; it has since rebounded to about $0.99 and is now the top gainer in the top 100 (up about 7.5% over 24 hours), with no specific trigger reported either way. The swings follow a choppy month: the token fell about 23% in the week to Oct. 19 after LayerZero and Stargate opened bridges letting holders move M to BNB Chain and Base, then bounced roughly 50%. On-chain investigator ZachXBT has previously accused insiders of manipulating the token's price, and a token unlock is due Nov. 1.
crypto.meaning: Moves of 20% in a day without clear news are typical of tokens where a few wallets hold much of the supply, so price can swing on a handful of trades. About 56 million new M tokens (roughly 2.5% of circulating supply) unlock on Nov. 1, which adds potential selling pressure.

outlook.bullCase: If the sell-off was one large holder exiting and the broader market steadies, it could rebound toward $1.05–$1.15, where it traded earlier this week.
outlook.bearCase: More large-wallet selling or selling ahead of the Nov. 1 unlock could push it toward $0.75–$0.80, its lows from mid-October.
outlook.watch: Large transfers to exchanges from top wallets, the Nov. 1 unlock, and whether the project explains the drop.

crypto.name: AKEDO
crypto.move: Up 9.8% in 24h, up 5.7% this week, at about $0.0319 (down 3.1% over 30 days)
crypto.why: AKEDO is a small AI-tools token that only just squeezed into CoinGecko's top 100. We could not find a clear news catalyst for its jump to about $0.039 late Friday, and that gain has now fully unwound: it has fallen about 20% from that peak to about $0.032 (up about 9% over the latest 24 hours), well below its old $0.037 ceiling and holding just above the $0.03 level we flagged. The slide comes days after a scheduled Oct. 21 unlock of tokens worth about $63 million (roughly 9% of its market value), and earlier community analysis found the top 100 wallets hold almost all of the supply, so a few holders can move the price sharply.
crypto.meaning: The failed breakout above $0.037 has turned into a slide of about a fifth, a reminder that a double-digit jump on no identifiable news, in a token with extremely concentrated ownership, can reverse quickly. Anyone holding it is exposed to large holders and freshly unlocked supply.

outlook.bullCase: Holding $0.03 and climbing back above the old $0.037 ceiling on steady volume would suggest the selling has run its course.
outlook.bearCase: A close below about $0.03 would open the way toward roughly $0.022, a level flagged as key support, especially if large holders or recipients of the Oct. 21 unlock keep selling.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds above about $0.03, trading volume, large-wallet transfers to exchanges, and any official project news.

crypto.name: NEAR Protocol
crypto.move: Up 2.6% in 24h, down 8.3% this week, at about $4.57 (down 6.5% over 30 days)
crypto.why: NEAR, the token of a fast smart-contract blockchain (one that runs apps), is up about 3% over the past day at about $4.52, and down about 10% over seven days. We could not find a fresh project-specific headline behind it; it looks like the same pattern seen across smaller coins this weekend, where traders using borrowed money get forced out as prices fall (a liquidation). The project is still carrying baggage from an Oct. 1 exploit that drained about $3.8 million from its NEAR Intents cross-chain service, which paused those services, per CoinDesk, and a whale's $2.6 million leveraged long was wiped out on Oct. 13 when it last tested this area.
crypto.meaning: NEAR has now slipped into the $4.40–$4.50 zone traders flagged as key support in mid-October, and it is down about 10% this week. Holders should expect sharp swings in thin weekend trading; the token tends to fall harder than bitcoin when the market turns cautious.

outlook.bullCase: If bitcoin steadies after next Wednesday's Fed decision and NEAR reclaims about $4.85–$5, the drop would look like a shake-out, opening a path back toward the mid-October highs above $5.
outlook.bearCase: A daily close well below $4.40–$4.50 would break the support analysts have watched since mid-October and could open a slide toward roughly $3.90–$4.
outlook.watch: Whether $4.40–$4.50 holds through the weekend, bitcoin's direction around $80,000, any update on the NEAR Intents exploit recovery, and futures liquidation data.

crypto.name: Zcash
crypto.move: Up 3.1% in 24h, up 7.2% this week, at about $1,241 (down 20.1% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Traders had been positioning for the NU7 upgrade, which developers scheduled for about 7:50 p.m. ET on Nov. 5; it cuts block times from 75 to 25 seconds and sends 60% of fees to a reserve. Futures open interest (the value of open bets) had risen about 19–24% and two large traders reportedly opened about $37.6 million of 10x leveraged longs. Those leveraged bets have been unwinding: CoinDesk flagged ZEC among the coins where bullish traders were closing positions, and CoinDesk noted an 8% drop in open interest Friday, and after dipping below the $1,190–$1,230 support area, the price has bounced back above it, to about $1,206 (roughly flat over 24 hours).
crypto.meaning: Much of this month's rally was driven by borrowed money, and this week shows how fast that can reverse. Upgrade dates often bring 'buy the rumour, sell the news' behaviour, so swings both ways are likely into Nov. 5.

outlook.bullCase: Holding the $1,180–$1,200 area and renewed interest as the upgrade nears could bring it back to the $1,375 resistance and, beyond that, the September high near $1,700.
outlook.bearCase: Losing $1,180 would erase the October breakout and could send it toward about $1,000–$1,120, near its 50-day average.
outlook.watch: The $1,180 level, funding rates and open interest, ETF flows, and any upgrade delay.

crypto.name: Solana
crypto.move: Up 1.0% in 24h, down 3.1% this week, at about $101.66 (down 15.7% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Solana completed its Alpenglow upgrade, a major overhaul aimed at much faster transaction finality (the point at which a payment can't be reversed), according to CoinDesk. The price has moved with the market rather than rallying on the news, and it slipped under $100 Saturday morning as bitcoin's break below $80,000 triggered forced selling across crypto, briefly tested $100 again in Asian trading Monday, and it is about $101.66 at 8:35 a.m.
crypto.meaning: A smooth Alpenglow launch is a meaningful technical milestone, but the market is treating it as already expected. The first days after a big upgrade are when problems usually show up, so stability matters more than headlines.

outlook.bullCase: A trouble-free upgrade and stronger crypto risk appetite could lift SOL back toward $115–$120.
outlook.bearCase: Any outage or bug after the upgrade, or bitcoin staying below $80,000, could push SOL toward $90.
outlook.watch: Whether SOL regains $100, network stability after Alpenglow, bitcoin's $80,000 level, and Solana ETF flows.

stocks.name: S&P 500
stocks.move: Closed down 0.5% (40 points) at 7,624 Friday, its second straight weekly loss; about 2.8% below its record near 7,845
stocks.why: Oil and yields back near 5% weighed on the index, and nearly three in four S&P 500 stocks fell, per AP. Banks, telecoms, industrials and consumer names led the decline while energy (ConocoPhillips up 3.6%, Chevron up 2.9%) and chips gained; the University of Michigan's final October consumer sentiment reading slipped to 48.0, near a record low, with year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.7%.
stocks.meaning: The damage is concentrated in tech, which makes up a large share of the index, while other sectors are holding up better. Falling bond yields help a little, but a 10-year yield near 5% still makes stocks look expensive relative to bonds.

outlook.bullCase: Solid results from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon next week, a calm Fed on Oct. 28 and yields easing further could carry it back toward the 7,845 record.
outlook.bearCase: A deeper tech sell-off, a hawkish Fed, or an oil spike above $115 could drag it below 7,600 toward the 7,500 area.
outlook.watch: Whether 7,600 holds early next week, oil prices, and the Fed decision on Oct. 28 followed by Microsoft and Alphabet earnings that evening.

stocks.name: Verizon
stocks.move: Up about 2% before the bell Monday after results, from Friday's close of $44.66 (down 1.2% Friday)
stocks.why: Verizon reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.31 a share at 7 a.m., above the roughly $1.27–$1.28 analysts expected, and added 406,000 net postpaid phone subscribers (monthly-bill phone customers), its best in years. Revenue of $34.3 billion, up 1.5%, came in below the roughly $34.8 billion forecast. It raised its 2026 outlook for subscriber additions (now 1.1–1.2 million), adjusted earnings ($5.04–$5.06 a share) and free cash flow growth (about 12%), and a report says it signed an AI infrastructure deal with Amazon Web Services worth more than $2 billion.
stocks.meaning: The results suggest Verizon's turnaround in customer growth is real, which supports its dividend (a yield above 6%). The overhang is SpaceX's push toward becoming a fourth carrier, which knocked telecom stocks down sharply this month, so strong numbers may not fully lift the stock while that threat is unresolved.

outlook.bullCase: If the earnings beat and raised guidance hold up through the call and the open, a daily close above about $45.70 (its moving averages) could open the way toward $48.
outlook.bearCase: If investors focus on the revenue miss, or SpaceX signs tower deals, the stock could slip back below $43.07 support toward about $40.30.
outlook.watch: How the stock trades after the open, management's comments on the call about competition and SpaceX, any signed SpaceX tower leases, and AT&T and T-Mobile reactions.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.move: Closed down 1.0% at about $642.60, after Thursday's 7% drop; it touched $633 early Friday
stocks.why: Third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, beating forecasts, and fourth-quarter guidance topped estimates, but the stock fell as investors focus on costs: Meta expects $135–$145 billion of capital spending, free cash flow was about -$2.1 billion this quarter, and a $9.9 billion legal charge cut reported profit. It also surprised Wall Street with a new non-voting Class C share, one for every share held starting in January 2027; JPMorgan's Doug Anmuth called the pending shares an overhang (a supply worry hanging over the price) and urged Meta to issue any new stock quickly. Meta's filing says the Class C dividend is expected to work like a two-for-one stock split for Class A holders.
stocks.meaning: The core ad business is growing fast, which supports the stock, but AI spending pushed free cash flow negative (about -$2.1 billion) this quarter. A separate $25 billion penalty imposed by a New Mexico judge in a privacy case is under appeal and adds legal uncertainty.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.move: Closed down 0.6% at about $372, after touching $365 early; down 3.1% Thursday
stocks.why: Tesla rose during the day on Musk's comments that Tesla and SpaceX formed committees to study a merger. After the close it reported adjusted earnings of $0.48 a share versus about $0.45 expected and revenue of $28.05 billion, flat from a year ago and slightly below some forecasts; free cash flow of $1.5 billion beat expectations of a cash burn because spending came in about $3 billion lower than expected. Shares fell about 5% before the open as Tesla cut its 2026 capital-spending plan to about $20 billion from more than $25 billion and Musk said reaching 20,000 Optimus robots a week will take at least a year. Buyers erased the early loss after the open, but it slipped again as the Nasdaq weakened and closed near the day's low.
stocks.meaning: The core business is weak: operating income fell 56% to $718 million and deliveries slipped 2%, so the stock still trades mostly on robotaxi, Optimus and SpaceX-merger hopes. Lower spending helps cash flow but can read as a slower AI push, which explains the early selling.

outlook.bullCase: Concrete merger progress or a smooth Cybercab expansion to Dallas next month could bring it back toward $400–$410.
outlook.bearCase: If the early dip resumes and analysts trim targets, it could slide back toward $355–$375.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds the $365 area, merger committee news, and the NHTSA Cybercab response due Oct. 30.
